turns.text: Hi, thanks for joining. Can you walk me through a retrieval system you've built end to end?

Sure. The AI Study Assistant ingests lecture notes, chunks them by heading, embeds with a hosted embedding model and stores them in pgvector. At query time we do hybrid search, rerank the top 20, and pass the top 5 to Claude with citations.
How did you evaluate retrieval quality?

I built a set of about 150 question and answer pairs from past exams and tracked recall at 5 and answer faithfulness. Moving from fixed-size chunks to heading-based chunks took recall at 5 from 0.71 to 0.86.
What would you do differently in TypeScript versus Python for this stack?
The web app and streaming UI are TypeScript with Next.js. I kept ingestion in TypeScript too so there's one type system, but I'd move heavy batch embedding to a Python worker if volume grew.
Tell me about a time a model output caused a production problem.
Early on the bot answered confidently when retrieval returned nothing relevant. I added a relevance threshold and a 'not in your notes' response, and logged those cases to improve coverage.
Great, that's all my questions. Anything you'd like to ask?
Just what the team's eval process looks like today. Thanks!
